'''Runaway Prince''', or '''Lordunkee Wanpolla''' in [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], was a minor [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] colony [[Planet/Legends|world]] in a [[Hutt Space/Legends|region]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] controlled by the Hutt [[Species/Legends|species]]. During the early stages of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the planet was one of several worlds promised to the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extragalactic]] invaders, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], by the Hutts as a token of goodwill and for resource gathering.

==Description==
Runaway Prince was a terrestrial<ref name="JE" /> [[Planet/Legends|world]]<ref name="EA" /> located in the [[Runaway Prince system/Legends|eponymous star system]].<ref name="EAOC" /> The planet was a part of the [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]<ref name="JE" /><ref name="EA" /> situated within [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Runaway Prince lay between two major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] – the [[Oktos Route]] and ''[[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|Ootmian Pabol]]''.<ref name="EA" />

==History==
===Part of Hutt Space===
The cosmic space surrounding the planet was explored sometime between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15000]] and [[8000 BBY]]. By the time the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] erupted across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the planet was already located within a [[Hutt Space/Legends|region]] of space controlled by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The Hutts established a minor [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] on the planet, which had been known by the peculiar name «Lordunkee Wanpolla» for as long as the Hutts could remember. The name translated into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] as «Runaway Prince», although the story behind its origin had long since been forgotten.<ref name="EA" />

===Treaty world===
{{Quote|Let us talk business. As&hellip; Pedric Cuf has undoubtedly apprised you, the Yuuzhan Vong have need of some of your worlds—for purposes of resource gathering. To effect this, we may be required to remove entire populations, and in some cases remake those worlds we select.|[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Malik Carr]], to [[Borga Besadii Diori|Borga the Hutt]]|<ref name="JE" />}}
During [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|extragalactic]] race of invaders, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], launched a massive [[Yuuzhan Vong War|conquest campaign]] directed against all worlds of the [[Galactic community]].<ref name="VP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]''</ref> [[26 ABY/Legends|Less than a year later]],<ref name="IYV">{{GamerCite|8|I, Yuuzhan Vong}}</ref> the Yuuzhan Vong had provided numerous examples showing that those populations who mounted resistance saw their worlds poisoned or devastated. Nonetheless, some Hutts believe that they can remain neutral in the war with the invaders, selling [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to the Yuuzhan Vong, arms to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], and [[Spice/Legends|spice]] to nearly everyone else.<ref name="NJOS">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''</ref>

[[File:BorgaAndHutts.jpg|left|thumb|250px|By the treaty with the Yuuzhan Vong, the Hutts agreed to turn over one of their worlds to the invaders]]
The Yuuzhan Vong agitator [[Nom Anor]], operating under the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Ooglith masquer|guise]] of Pedric Cuf, proposed terms under which the Hutts would refrain from fighting the Yuuzhan Vong and turn over several worlds for resource gathering, even if doing so required the invaders to remove entire populations and, in some cases, [[Terraforming/Legends|reshape]] the worlds. The Hutt [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidics]] and [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Grand Council]] empowered [[Borga Besadii Diori]] to negotiate with Yuuzhan Vong [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Malik Carr]] on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]]. The Hutts agreed to the terms of the invaders, and, in exchange, the Yuuzhan Vong allowed the Hutts to continue trading freely while informing them which worlds to avoid, thereby reducing the likelihood of conflicts of interest.<ref name="JE" />

In accordance with the terms, the Hutts ceded one of the selected worlds, Runaway Prince, to the Yuuzhan Vong.<ref name="JE" /> Located near the outermost borders of Hutt Space,<ref name="EA" /> the planet was subsequently reshaped by the Yuuzhan Vong for the cultivation of biotechnology, including the sowing of [[yorik coral]], [[villip]] shrubs, and other resources required for the war effort.<ref name="JE" />

===Later fate===
Shortly thereafter, after the Hutts provided the New Republic with secret information, the Yuuzhan Vong [[Battle of Fondor|suffered]] a major military calamity near [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]]. In response, the [[Supreme Commander (Yuuzhan Vong rank)|Supreme Commander]] [[Nas Choka]] turned the wrath of the Yuuzhan Vong against their former allies.<ref name="JE" /> Nas Choka swiftly conquered Hutt Space,<ref name="CEH">{{CSWECite|II|68|Hutt}}</ref> bringing the former Hutt holdings to the brink of ruin and reshaping many of their worlds. Hutt Space, including Runaway Prince, remained under Yuuzhan Vong control until the end of the war,<ref name="EA" /> when the invaders surrendered under the terms of the [[Sekot accords]].<ref name="UP">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The planet Runaway Prince first appeared in the novel ''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]'', which was written by [[James Luceno]] and released in [[2000]].<ref name="JE" /> Later, Runaway Prince was mentioned in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', a [[2009]] reference book co-authored by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]], which placed the planet in grid square R-11.<ref name="EA" />

The [[2008]] reference guide ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' introduced an inaccuracy by stating that Borga the Hutt tried to negotiate a treaty with the Yuuzhan Vong, «ostensibly offering up one world in Hutt space»,<ref name="CEH" /> whereas in the novel ''Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse'', the invaders demanded several worlds for their own purposes<ref name="JE" /> and in fact received at least one world, Runaway Prince.<ref name="JE" /><ref name="NJOS" />
